title: zero-dimensional etale cohomology degree-zero stalk comparison
statement:
Let u be a universe, k : Type u an algebraically closed field, C : Scheme.{u}, and f : C ⟶ Spec k a separated, locally finite-type, quasi-compact morphism. Assume topologicalKrullDim C ≤ 0. Let F be a sheaf of abelian groups in universe u+1 on the small étale site of C. For each underlying point x : C choose an algebraically closed field Ω(x) : Type u and a morphism s(x) : Spec Ω(x) ⟶ C whose unique source point maps to x. No algebraicity of Ω(x) over k or extra linearity condition on s(x) is assumed. Then the canonical degree-zero comparison followed by restriction to the identity etale object and the product of germs at s(x) is an isomorphism. Its exact composite is the Lean signature below.

Exact Lean signature:
theorem zero_dimensional_etale_cohomology_iso
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (C : Scheme.{u})
    (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [QuasiCompact f] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim C ≤ 0)
    (F : Sheaf C.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (Ω : C → Type u) [∀ x, Field (Ω x)] [∀ x, IsAlgClosed (Ω x)]
    (s : ∀ x : C, Spec (.of (Ω x)) ⟶ C)
    (hs : ∀ x : C, (s x).base.hom default = x) :
    IsIso ((Functor.homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso
        (Sheaf.Γ C.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) F 0).hom ≫
          (Functor.rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf
            (Sheaf.Γ C.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).hom.app F ≫
          F.ΓRes (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 C))) ≫ Pi.lift (fun x : C =>
            (Scheme.pointSmallEtale (s x)).toPresheafFiber
              (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 C))
              (Over.homMk (s x) (Category.comp_id (s x))) F.obj))

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian], the finite-type
zero-dimensional scheme $C$ has finite discrete underlying space and every
point is closed. Let $i:C_{\mathrm{red}}\to C$ be the reduction. By
[lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced
and $i$ is a universal homeomorphism. Since $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a closed
subscheme of the finite-type $k$-scheme $C$, it is itself finite type over $k$.
Applying [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] to $C_{\mathrm{red}}$
identifies every residue field $\kappa_{C_{\mathrm{red}}}(c)$ with $k$ (equivalently,
$\mathcal O_{C_{\mathrm{red}},c}=\mathcal O_{C,c}/\sqrt{0}$ has the same
residue field). The singleton pieces of the finite discrete space
$C_{\mathrm{red}}$ are open and closed. Each such piece is affine by
[lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-affine]. Its coordinate ring is reduced
and has only one prime, hence is a field; the residue-field identification
makes that field $k$. Therefore each piece is $\operatorname{Spec}k$. By
[lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], the morphism from the coproduct of
these pieces to $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ induced by their inclusions is an
isomorphism: its restriction to each summand is the corresponding open
immersion, and the summands are pairwise disjoint and cover $C_{\mathrm{red}}$,
so it is bijective and a local isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-geometric-point-coproduct-cohomology] to the finite coproduct obtained in step 1 and the restriction of F. The degree-zero canonical product-of-germs morphism is invertible. The chosen geometric points s(x) factor uniquely through the reduction, since Spec Ω(x) is reduced. On each Spec k summand, apply [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] with R = k to both the canonical k-point and the specified geometric point. Both natural germ maps from sections are isomorphisms. Composing the inverse canonical germ with the specified germ gives the stalk comparison and identifies the canonical product-of-germs map with the specified product-of-germs map. No assumption that Ω(x) is algebraic over k is needed.

source.place: Lemma 03QO for both natural germ isomorphisms; Lemma 0A5B, first proof paragraph, for finite coproduct cohomology

proof.text: Use [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] for i : C_red → C from [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] to transport all cohomology groups of the inverse image of F to those of F. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] to i and the lift of each specified s(x). Its germ formula identifies the product of pulled-back germs with the product of germs at s(x), after the unit comparison and the point bijection. Naturality of the degree-zero derived-to-underived comparison and restriction to the terminal étale object therefore identifies the transported isomorphism with exactly the displayed Lean composite. This proves the specified degree-zero composite invertible without assuming finiteness or reducedness of C.
